title: Deckhand configuration
description: The shape of dashboard.json and dashboard.local.json. The local file is merged over the shared one on load: keys in it win, objects merge a level at a time, and a list or plain value replaces the shared one outright.

columns.description: How many columns the dashboard width is divided into.

rows.description: How many rows the dashboard height is divided into. Rows share the height equally; at 12 rows a row is shorter than a tile, so one-row groups scroll from the start.

enabled.description: Whether starting up asks 'laptop or tablet?'. Off, nothing listens and the token is never read. --remote on the command line serves regardless; this only decides whether the question is asked.

listen.description: The HttpListener prefix to serve on. '+' is every interface; narrow it to one address, or to http://127.0.0.1:8787/ behind a tunnel.

token.description: Don't put the token here — this file travels with the project. Keep it in the token file instead, which wins over this whenever it has anything in it.

tokenFile.description: Where the token really lives: one line, nothing else. Defaults to %USERPROFILE%\.deckhand_token.

allowedHosts.description: Names (besides addresses, which need no permission) the panel may be reached by — a Tailscale name, a tunnel's hostname. A name has to be listed because what it points at isn't ours to decide.

browsers.description: Process names that count as a browser, for URL tiles opening in the focused one. Defaults to chrome, msedge, firefox, brave, vivaldi, opera, opera_gx.

profiles.description: Names for the apps worth recognising. A profile holds no tiles — sections written for its label appear while it's the focused app. First match wins, so order most-specific first.

match.description: Process names that activate this profile, with or without .exe. Case-insensitive.

titleMatch.description: Optional regex the window title must also match, for splitting one app into several profiles.

sections.description: Every button on the dashboard. A section with no profiles is always on screen; one that lists them shows only while a matching app is focused.

profiles.description: Profile labels this section belongs to. Omit for a section that's always shown.

tilesPerRow.description: Tiles per row inside this section. Defaults to the section's width in columns.

apps.description: Shorthand for a single always-visible "Apps" section.

snippets.description: Shorthand for a single always-visible "Snippets" section.

sourceSettings.description: Fills the section with one tile per subdirectory of a folder. With a "command" the tiles type it into the focused window (gate the section with "profiles" naming the windows it types into — the tap re-checks that list); without one, tapping opens the folder itself.

folders.description: The directory whose subdirectories become tiles. %VARIABLES% are expanded.

exclude.description: Directory names to leave out of the scan.

split.description: A regex (case-insensitive) dealing the folders onto the two sides of the section's ⇄ switch: matches on one, the rest on the other. Its first capture group becomes {id} in the commands. Omitted, there is no switch.

matchLabel.description: What the ⇄ switch calls the folders "split" matches.

otherLabel.description: What the ⇄ switch calls the rest.

command.description: Typed into the focused window on tap. {name} is the folder's name, {id} what "split" captured, {dir} the full path. Omit it and tapping opens the folder instead, like an app tile pointed at it.

submit.description: Press Enter after typing, so the command runs rather than just sitting there.

commands.description: Extra commands reached by expanding a tile with its ▾. None means no ▾.

commandColumns.description: Columns in a tile's expanded command list.

max.description: Cap on folder tiles. The section header says when tiles were dropped.

subtitles.description: A file — or a glob like "%USERPROFILE%/notes/titles_*" — of "key|text" lines. A folder whose {id} (or name) appears as a key gets the text as a second line on its tile. The format is the whole contract; anything can write it.

gridRange.description: A width (3 — packed into the first gap that fits) or a pinned 1-based range ("1-3" — those tracks, wherever the other sections end up).

path.description: A program, a folder, or an http(s) URL — a URL opens as a new tab rather than launching anything.

args.description: Command line for the program. On a URL tile these are browser switches, applied only when a browser is named.

browser.description: URL tiles only. Omit for the focused browser, "default" for the default one, or a process name like "msedge" to pin it.

deElevate.description: Launch at normal user integrity instead of inheriting the dashboard's elevation. On by default; set false on the rare tile that should run elevated on purpose.

windows.description: Process names whose windows the tile goes to, for when the thing launched isn't the thing that ends up on screen (git-bash.exe starts a mintty and exits).

span.description: How many of the section's tile columns this tile occupies.

text.description: Dropped at the caret. \n is a newline, so the editor's auto-indent applies per line. {date}, {time} and {clipboard} are resolved at the moment of the tap: the local short date and time, and whatever text is on the clipboard.

method.description: "paste" goes via the clipboard and Ctrl+V; "type" is sent a character at a time and leaves the clipboard alone.

keys.description: Keys pressed after the text lands, in order: "tab", "enter", "escape", separated by spaces or commas.

span.description: How many of the section's tile columns this tile occupies.

tileColor.description: Accent for the tile's outline, on the panel and the tablet alike: #RGB or #RRGGBB — the two forms WPF and a browser agree about.

tileIcon.description: A picture for the tile: the path to a png, jpg, gif, bmp, ico, webp or svg file — the types the panel and the tablet can both draw. An svg must be self-contained: one pointing at another file, declaring entities or carrying script is refused at load. webp is the one whose decoder Windows keeps optional, so a machine without the Web Media Extensions component draws the label instead. Absolute, or relative to this file's own folder, with %ENVVARS% expanded. Nothing is extracted or fetched: the tile draws the file named here and no other.

tileIconMode.description: Where the picture goes: "left" of the label; "above" it, the picture taking the tile with the label underneath; or "fill", the tile being the picture with the label kept as its tooltip. An app tile's + is never a picture whichever this is.
